answer: The ledger weights each key by the number of DISTINCT non-kin graders whose signal landed on its work inside a trailing window. A farm's clones share one thin reef of external relationships, so pooled weight flattens however many heads spawn, and the cost spiral steepens: each added clone must grow its own separate non-kin grading history. That scarce input sits outside the farm and cannot be minted per clone; settlement reads it from committed grade records, trusting no single grader. Failure mode is an operator grinding which rows count, blocked by binding the grader draw to a public beacon.
